The device acquires an image of the area surrounding the vehicle by means of an image acquisition unit. This peripheral image may include roads, sidewalks, intersections, parking areas, or other regions around the vehicle in which moving objects may be present.

An image extraction unit then processes the acquired peripheral image and extracts image data corresponding to at least one moving object. In particular, the image extraction unit may extract an image of the upper body, the lower body, or both the upper body and the lower body of the moving object. The moving object may be, for example, a pedestrian, cyclist, or other person located in the vicinity of the vehicle.

Based on the extracted image data, a moving object information determination unit determines information relating to the moving object. This information may include whether the moving object is present or absent in the vehicle’s surroundings, and, when present, the position of the moving object relative to the vehicle.

The upper body image extracted by the image extraction unit is not limited to an image showing the entire upper body of the moving object. The upper body image may include the whole upper body, or it may include only a portion of the upper body, such as the head, shoulders, torso, arms, or any combination thereof.

Similarly, the lower body image is not limited to an image showing the entire lower body of the moving object. The lower body image may include the whole lower body, or it may include only a portion of the lower body, such as the waist, legs, feet, or any combination thereof.
outputs.L4:
A vehicle moving-body information device is provided for detecting and identifying moving objects located around a vehicle. The device acquires images of the area surrounding the vehicle by using one or more imaging units, such as onboard cameras directed toward the front, rear, sides, or other peripheral regions of the vehicle. From the acquired peripheral images, the device extracts image portions corresponding to moving objects, including images of an upper body, a lower body, or portions thereof. For example, the device may detect a pedestrian even when only the pedestrian’s legs are visible behind another vehicle, or when only the upper body is captured above an obstacle.

The extracted upper-body and/or lower-body images are analyzed to determine whether a moving object is present in the vicinity of the vehicle. The device may also determine positional information of the moving object, such as its location relative to the vehicle, its direction of movement, or its approximate distance. By using partial body images rather than requiring a complete image of the moving object, the device can recognize pedestrians, cyclists, or other moving bodies under conditions where visibility is limited or the object is partially occluded.

This approach improves the ability of the vehicle to monitor its surroundings in real time. It is particularly useful in traffic environments where pedestrians or other moving objects may be hidden by parked cars, roadside structures, other vehicles, or blind spots. The resulting moving-body information can be supplied to a driver assistance system, warning system, autonomous driving controller, or collision avoidance system. As a result, the vehicle can provide earlier warnings, support safer driving decisions, and enhance overall situational awareness and safety.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style embodiment description for a vehicle device that detects moving objects from peripheral images by extracting upper-body and/or lower-body images and determining presence or position.
counterfactuals.output:
In one embodiment, a vehicle-mounted object detection device is provided for detecting a moving object existing around a vehicle based on peripheral images captured from the vehicle. The vehicle-mounted object detection device includes an image acquisition unit, an image processing unit, an extraction unit, and a determination unit.

The image acquisition unit acquires peripheral images of an area around the vehicle. The peripheral images may be captured by one or more imaging devices mounted on the vehicle, such as a front camera, a rear camera, a side camera, a fisheye camera, or a surround-view camera. The peripheral images may include images of a road surface, sidewalks, intersections, parking areas, or regions adjacent to the vehicle.

The image processing unit performs preprocessing on the acquired peripheral images. The preprocessing may include distortion correction, viewpoint conversion, brightness correction, contrast adjustment, noise reduction, edge enhancement, or generation of a bird’s-eye-view image. In some examples, the image processing unit extracts candidate regions from the peripheral images by detecting motion, contours, feature points, optical flow, differences between temporally successive frames, or regions having image characteristics corresponding to a person, cyclist, animal, or other moving object.

The extraction unit extracts, from the peripheral images or from the candidate regions, at least one of an upper-body image and a lower-body image of a moving object. The upper-body image may include an image portion corresponding to a head, shoulders, torso, arms, or an upper portion of a person. The lower-body image may include an image portion corresponding to legs, feet, a lower torso, or a lower portion of a person. The extraction unit may extract the upper-body image and/or the lower-body image by using pattern matching, machine-learning classification, a trained neural network, template comparison, skeletal estimation, body-part segmentation, or feature extraction based on shape, color, texture, edge direction, or motion.

In one embodiment, the extraction unit extracts an upper-body candidate region from the peripheral image and determines whether the upper-body candidate region satisfies an upper-body condition. The upper-body condition may include at least one of a predetermined aspect ratio, a predetermined size range, a head-shoulder contour, a torso-like shape, a motion pattern, or a confidence value output by a classifier. Similarly, the extraction unit may extract a lower-body candidate region from the peripheral image and determine whether the lower-body candidate region satisfies a lower-body condition. The lower-body condition may include at least one of a leg-like shape, a periodic walking motion, a pair of vertically extending regions, a foot-region feature, or a confidence value output by a classifier.

The determination unit determines the presence of the moving object based on the extracted upper-body image and/or the extracted lower-body image. For example, when either the upper-body image or the lower-body image satisfies a predetermined reliability condition, the determination unit may determine that a moving object is present. Alternatively, when both the upper-body image and the lower-body image are extracted in a positional relationship corresponding to a human body, the determination unit may determine that the moving object is a pedestrian. The positional relationship may include alignment in a vertical direction of the image, relative distance between the upper-body image and the lower-body image, overlap or adjacency of bounding regions, or consistency with a projected ground-plane position.

In another embodiment, the determination unit determines a position of the moving object relative to the vehicle based on the extracted upper-body image and/or lower-body image. The position may be determined by converting coordinates of the extracted image region into real-world coordinates using camera calibration information, a road surface model, a viewpoint transformation, stereo distance information, structure-from-motion information, or size-based distance estimation. The determined position may include at least one of a lateral position, a longitudinal position, a distance from the vehicle, an azimuth angle, a relative velocity, or a predicted path.

The device may further include a tracking unit configured to track the moving object across a plurality of frames. The tracking unit may associate an extracted upper-body image and/or lower-body image in a current frame with a corresponding region in a previous frame. Tracking may be performed using optical flow, Kalman filtering, particle filtering, feature matching, bounding-box association, or a neural-network-based tracker. The determination unit may update the presence or position of the moving object based on the tracking result.

In one example, when a lower portion of a pedestrian is hidden by another vehicle, a roadside object, or an image boundary, the device may determine the presence and/or position of the pedestrian based on the extracted upper-body image. Conversely, when an upper portion of the pedestrian is obscured or outside the field of view, the device may determine the presence and/or position of the pedestrian based on the extracted lower-body image. Thus, the device can improve detection robustness even when only part of the moving object is visible in the peripheral image.

In another example, the determination unit compares a detection result based on the upper-body image with a detection result based on the lower-body image. When the two detection results are consistent, the determination unit may increase a reliability value associated with the detected moving object. When the two detection results are inconsistent, the determination unit may select one of the detection results based on confidence values, image quality, occlusion estimation, distance from the vehicle, or temporal continuity.

The vehicle-mounted object detection device may output the determined presence or position of the moving object to a vehicle control device, a driver assistance device, a display device, or an alarm device. Based on the output, the vehicle may perform or assist with warning generation, collision avoidance, automatic braking, steering assistance, parking assistance, blind-spot monitoring, pedestrian detection, or autonomous driving control.

The moving object detected by the device may include, but is not limited to, a pedestrian, a cyclist, a person riding a small mobility vehicle, an animal, or another object having an upper portion and/or a lower portion detectable in the peripheral image. The extraction and determination processing may be executed by a processor using software stored in memory, by dedicated hardware circuitry, or by a combination thereof. The device may be implemented as an electronic control unit mounted in the vehicle, as part of an advanced driver assistance system, or as part of an autonomous driving system.

counterfactuals.output:
The following is exemplary formal patent-style language for a **device for providing moving body information for a vehicle**.

---

## Title  
**Device for Providing Moving Body Information for a Vehicle**

## Abstract  
A device for providing moving body information for a vehicle is disclosed. The device includes an image acquisition unit configured to acquire image data corresponding to surroundings of the vehicle, an image extraction unit configured to extract, from the acquired image data, image information corresponding to at least one moving body, and a moving object information determination unit configured to determine moving body information of the at least one moving body based on the extracted image information. The moving body information may include at least one of a position, speed, moving direction, type, distance from the vehicle, and predicted movement path of the moving body. The device may provide the determined moving body information to a vehicle control system, driver assistance system, display unit, or warning unit.

---

## Detailed Description  

A device for providing moving body information for a vehicle may be mounted in, installed on, or operatively connected to a vehicle. The device is configured to detect and provide information regarding one or more moving bodies located around the vehicle. The moving body may include, for example, another vehicle, a pedestrian, a cyclist, a motorcycle, an animal, or any other object capable of movement in a surrounding environment of the vehicle.

The device may include an image acquisition unit, an image extraction unit, and a moving object information determination unit.

The image acquisition unit may be configured to acquire image data of an area surrounding the vehicle. The image acquisition unit may include at least one camera, image sensor, infrared camera, stereo camera, wide-angle camera, or other optical sensing device. The image acquisition unit may acquire image data corresponding to a front area, rear area, side area, or omnidirectional area around the vehicle. In some embodiments, the image acquisition unit may acquire sequential image frames at predetermined time intervals.

The image extraction unit may be configured to receive the image data acquired by the image acquisition unit and extract image information corresponding to a moving body included in the image data. The image extraction unit may identify a region of interest, boundary, contour, feature point, object candidate region, motion region, or pixel group associated with the moving body. The image extraction unit may extract the image information using at least one of motion detection, background subtraction, optical flow, edge detection, object recognition, pattern matching, machine learning, or a neural network-based image processing technique.

The moving object information determination unit may be configured to determine moving body information based on the image information extracted by the image extraction unit. The moving body information may include at least one of a type of the moving body, a location of the moving body relative to the vehicle, a distance between the moving body and the vehicle, a speed of the moving body, a moving direction of the moving body, an acceleration of the moving body, a moving trajectory, a predicted path, and a risk level associated with the moving body.

In some embodiments, the moving object information determination unit may compare image information extracted from a plurality of temporally successive image frames to determine a change in position of the moving body over time. The moving object information determination unit may calculate the speed and moving direction of the moving body based on the change in position and a time interval between the image frames.

The device may further include an output unit configured to output the moving body information. The output unit may provide the moving body information to at least one of a driver assistance system, an autonomous driving controller, a vehicle control unit, a display device, a warning device, a navigation device, or a communication device. The output unit may provide visual, audible, or tactile notification to an occupant of the vehicle when the moving body is determined to be located within a predetermined distance or to have a predicted path intersecting with a predicted path of the vehicle.

The device may improve recognition of moving bodies around the vehicle and may assist in collision avoidance, lane changing, parking, autonomous driving, or other vehicle safety functions.

---

## Claims  

### Claim 1  
A device for providing moving body information for a vehicle, the device comprising:  

an image acquisition unit configured to acquire image data corresponding to surroundings of the vehicle;  

an image extraction unit configured to extract, from the image data acquired by the image acquisition unit, image information corresponding to at least one moving body; and  

a moving object information determination unit configured to determine moving body information of the at least one moving body based on the image information extracted by the image extraction unit.

### Claim 2  
The device of claim 1, wherein the moving body information includes at least one of a position, a distance, a speed, a moving direction, an acceleration, a type, a trajectory, and a predicted movement path of the at least one moving body.

### Claim 3  
The device of claim 1, wherein the image acquisition unit comprises at least one camera configured to capture an image of at least one of a front area, a rear area, a lateral area, and an omnidirectional area around the vehicle.

### Claim 4  
The device of claim 1, wherein the image acquisition unit is configured to acquire a plurality of image frames in temporal sequence, and wherein the moving object information determination unit is configured to determine a movement state of the at least one moving body based on a positional change of the at least one moving body in the plurality of image frames.

### Claim 5  
The device of claim 1, wherein the image extraction unit is configured to extract a region of interest corresponding to the at least one moving body from the image data.

### Claim 6  
The device of claim 1, wherein the image extraction unit is configured to extract the image information using at least one of object recognition, motion detection, optical flow analysis, background subtraction, edge detection, feature point extraction, pattern matching, or neural network-based image processing.

### Claim 7  
The device of claim 1, wherein the moving object information determination unit is configured to determine a relative position of the at least one moving body with respect to the vehicle.

### Claim 8  
The device of claim 1, wherein the moving object information determination unit is configured to determine a risk level based on the moving body information.

### Claim 9  
The device of claim 8, further comprising an output unit configured to output warning information when the risk level satisfies a predetermined condition.

### Claim 10  
The device of claim 1, further comprising an output unit configured to provide the moving body information to at least one of a vehicle control unit, an autonomous driving control unit, a driver assistance system, a display unit, a warning unit, or a communication unit.

### Claim 11  
The device of claim 1, wherein the at least one moving body includes at least one of another vehicle, a pedestrian, a cyclist, a motorcycle, an animal, or an object moving in the surroundings of the vehicle.

### Claim 12  
The device of claim 1, wherein the moving object information determination unit is configured to predict whether a movement path of the at least one moving body intersects a movement path of the vehicle.

### Claim 13  
The device of claim 12, wherein the moving object information determination unit is further configured to generate collision risk information based on the predicted intersection between the movement path of the at least one moving body and the movement path of the vehicle.

### Claim 14  
The device of claim 1, wherein the moving object information determination unit is implemented by at least one processor configured to execute instructions stored in a memory.

### Claim 15  
A vehicle comprising the device for providing moving body information according to claim 1.

---

## Additional Independent Method Claim  

### Claim 16  
A method for providing moving body information for a vehicle, the method comprising:  

acquiring, by an image acquisition unit, image data corresponding to surroundings of the vehicle;  

extracting, by an image extraction unit, image information corresponding to at least one moving body from the acquired image data; and  

determining, by a moving object information determination unit, moving body information of the at least one moving body based on the extracted image information.

### Claim 17  
The method of claim 16, wherein determining the moving body information comprises determining at least one of a relative position, distance, speed, moving direction, type, trajectory, predicted movement path, or risk level of the at least one moving body.

---

## Computer-Readable Medium Claim  

### Claim 18  
A non-transitory computer-readable recording medium storing instructions that, when executed by at least one processor, cause the at least one processor to perform operations comprising:  

receiving image data corresponding to surroundings of a vehicle;  

extracting image information corresponding to at least one moving body from the image data; and  

determining moving body information of the at least one moving body based on the extracted image information.
